Alan Ferdman
 Vice Chairman
[family detail omitted][family detail omitted][family detail omitted] Alan is a retired Aerospace Engineer and Department Manager. He holds a Master of Science degree in Software Engineering and a Bachelor of Science in Computer Science. During his career he held senior positions at Litton Guidance & Control in Woodland Hills, the Jet Propulsion Laboratory in Pasadena and as an adjunct faculty member at National University. Alan has always believed in giving back to the community. He volunteered for LACO Parks and Recreation, served on numerous City of Santa Clarita Panels and Committees and is most well known as CEO of the Santa Clarita Community Council and Chair of the Canyon Country Advisory Committee, a position he has held since 2002. Alan’s commitment to lending a helping hand continues to grow. In addition to his role an Old Town Newhall Association Board Member, he serves as President of the Eagle Colligate Academy Charter School Foundation Board, Samuel Dixon Family Heath Center Board Treasurer, and Vice-Chair of the Santa Clarita Senior Center Advisory Council. Alan’s love of country, community and helping Santa Clarita residents is well known and reflects his motto, “Together We Can Make a Difference”.

Vote for Alan Ferdman for City Council
 by Santa Clarita Magazine | Oct 1, 2016 | Community 
[family detail omitted][family detail omitted][family detail omitted]
Alan retired after working at JPL for six years and Litton Guidance for 40 years as a Project and Department Manager. He holds a Master of Science in Software Engineering and Bachelor of Science in Computer Science.
For the past 14 years Alan has been Chair of the Canyon Country Advisory Committee, a non-profit corporation, serving the Santa Clarita Valley, by providing information on issues affecting our valley and assisting residents in obtaining city services. He is also currently; Vice-Chairperson of the Senior Center Advisory Council and Chairman of the Samuel Dixon Rubber Ducky Regatta Committee. In addition, Alan is a member of the Sunrise Rotary, Santa Clarita Elks, Mint Canyon Moose and Old West Masonic Lodges.[family detail omitted]
Alan has always been a community advocate. He volunteered with LA County providing North Oaks Park evening staff services for four years, served for 13 years as the Chair of the Santa Clarita Adult Sports Committee, was a member of the Emergency Winter Shelter Site Selection Task Force, the Santa Clarita Open Space Committee, Friends of Hart School District Committee for Measure SA, the COC Canyon Country Site Selection Committee, the Santa Clarita Material Recycling Facility Site Selection Committee, the City of Santa Clarita Open Space Financial Accountability and Audit Panel for five years and the Bridge-to-Home Homeless Shelter Task Force.
Alan firmly believes, “We are all residents of the Santa Clarita Valley.[family detail omitted]”
For more information about Alan Ferdman go to www.electalanferdman.com .

khts2016.passage:
Posted by: Chris McCrory 
 in Politics , Santa Clarita Latest News 
 January 24, 2016 - 12:23 pm 
 4 Comments 
 1,417 Views 
 A longtime resident of Santa Clarita is running for city council in hopes that he will change the way the city is run.
 Sponsored Articles
Don’t miss a thing. Get breaking Santa Clarita news alerts delivered right to your inbox. 
 Alan Ferdman, chair of the Canyon Country Advisory Committee, believes that the current city council has neglected several aspects of government that heavily affect the Santa Clarita Valley. 
 “We’ve seen the area change,” Ferdman said in an interview. “Change is inevitable. However, it seems like the city is headed in the wrong direction.” 
 Related Story: Arroyo Seco Junior High Teacher Launches Campaign For U.S. Senate 
 His platform focuses on three major bases: traffic congestion management, the elimination of backdoor deals, and an increased focus on public safety. 
 Traffic 
 “I don’t think anybody in Santa Clarita is going to say traffic is getting better,” Ferdman said. “We need to develop some ways to alleviate traffic congestion.” 
 He pointed out several areas in the city where traffic was particularly hard to navigate and promised to find solutions for the jams. 
 “We’ve been investigating and talking about these issues,” he said. “I’d be able to hit the ground running.” 
 Backdoor Deals 
 A central pillar of Ferdman’s campaign is transparency, and a perceived lack of openness about how the city is run. 
 He pointed out the electronic billboard issue that was voted on by the city council in 2014 as an example. 
 “When the billboard issue came up…they got a petition with 16,000 signatures against it,” said Ferdman. “But Bob Kellar said ‘they didn’t know what they were signing.” 
 Ferdman believes that there needs to be a change in policy for council sessions and the issues discussed. 
 “We need to stop that kind of stuff,” he said, “so that the public has an opportunity to speak.” 
 Public Safety 
 Ferdman believes that public safety should be a higher priority for the city. 
 “We’ve had an increase in homicide (in the past year)” said Ferdman. “We need to figure out every way we can to reduce sheriff response time.” 
 The Sheriff’s Department is not the only major public safety outlet that needs an increase, said Ferdman. Organizations ranging from the Los Angeles County Fire Department to community outreach programs also needed to be looked at. 
 “Public safety is all of the organizations finding ways to help people in danger find a way to escape those situations,” he said.
 About Ferdman 
 Ferdman is the chair of the Canyon Country Advisory Committee, an organization founded by Santa Clarita residents “who wish to make Canyon Country a better place to work, live and play,” according to the organization’s website . 
 “I’ve been involved in these issues since 2000,” said Ferdman. “I believe that i have done my homework in understanding the city, the city’s staff and its operations.” 
 He believes that as an elected official “you should be able to engage the public and find out what they want.” 
 His goal is to provide a direct link to between the people and their city government, and listen to their interests and needs when deciding policy. 
 “The only way to find out what the public wants is to ask them,” Ferdman said. “I want to provide that avenue of communication.”
